cards.hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic regulation causes calibration set non-representativeness, leading to coverage instability across physiological signal segments from different individuals.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Individual differences in baseline heart rate variability (HRV) and baroreflex sensitivity alter the conditional distribution of prediction errors, making a pooled calibration set unrepresentative for specific subjects' test segments.
cards.causal_path: Subject ID -> Baseline HRV (RMSSD) & Baroreflex Sensitivity -> Conditional Error Distribution Shift -> Calibration-Test Distribution Mismatch -> Coverage Deviation
control_variables: Include subject as random effect in conformal score model
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is driven by segment duration differences rather than subject physiology; shorter segments have noisier error estimates.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation correlates with segment length, not with subject-level HRV metrics.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage deviation on both subject RMSSD and segment length; subject RMSSD remains significant predictor after controlling for length.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows HRV explains 15-30% variance in ECG-derived respiration error distributions; expect similar magnitude for coverage deviation.
minimum_data_needed: Multi-subject physiological recordings (>=30 subjects) with simultaneous ECG and reference respiration
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with RMSSD < 20 ms will show coverage deviation > 5% from nominal 90% when using pooled calibration, while subjects with RMSSD > 50 ms will show deviation < 2%.
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between subject RMSSD and coverage deviation after segment-length adjustment (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_deviation ~ RMSSD + segment_length + (1|subject), test RMSSD coefficient != 0.
cards.falsification_test: Per-subject conformal calibration (separate calibration set per subject) eliminates coverage deviation across all subjects; if deviation persists, subject physiology is not the primary mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Sensor electrode-skin impedance drift during long recordings creates segment-dependent measurement noise that violates exchangeability assumptions of conformal prediction.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Increasing electrode-skin impedance over time attenuates signal amplitude and increases high-frequency noise, shifting the distribution of model residuals in later segments relative to the calibration set.
cards.causal_path: Recording Duration -> Electrode-Skin Impedance (kOhm) -> Signal Amplitude Attenuation & Noise Floor Rise -> Residual Distribution Shift -> Coverage Drop in Late Segments
control_variables: Include impedance as covariate in conformal score
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drops in later segments due to physiological fatigue (e.g., decreasing HRV), not sensor degradation.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation correlates with physiological fatigue markers (e.g., HRV decline), not with impedance.
cards.distinguishing_test: Simultaneously track impedance and HRV; impedance predicts coverage deviation after controlling for HRV.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Impedance can increase 2-5x over 24h; prior studies show 3x impedance increase doubles ECG noise power, which should substantially shift residual distributions.
minimum_data_needed: Long-duration recordings (>=8h) with continuous impedance monitoring
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with impedance > 20 kOhm will show coverage < 85% at nominal 90%, while segments < 5 kOhm maintain coverage > 88%.
cards.failure_condition: No significant association between segment impedance and coverage deviation after controlling for time-on-task (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Generalized additive model: coverage ~ s(impedance) + s(time) + subject_random_effect, test significance of impedance smooth term.
cards.falsification_test: Artificially add noise to early segments to match late-segment noise characteristics; if coverage equalizes, sensor noise is the mechanism. If not, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary physiological dynamics during state transitions (sleep-wake, rest-exercise) create distribution shifts that violate the i.i.d. assumption within calibration segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Autonomic state transitions cause abrupt changes in signal morphology and variability, making residuals from one physiological state non-exchangeable with residuals from another state within the same calibration set.
cards.causal_path: Physiological State Transition -> Autonomic Balance Shift (LF/HF Ratio) -> Signal Morphology Change -> Residual Distribution Multimodality -> Conformal Quantile Miscalibration -> Coverage Instability
mechanism_variables: Signal Morphology Features (QRS width, T-wave amplitude)
control_variables: Include LF/HF as difficulty score in weighted conformal
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from label noise during state transitions (ambiguous ground truth), not from physiological non-stationarity.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation correlates with label uncertainty metrics, not with LF/HF ratio or morphology change magnitude.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage deviation in cleanly labeled stable-state segments vs. transition segments; physiological mechanism predicts deviation in stable states with different LF/HF, label-noise mechanism predicts deviation only at transitions.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Sleep-stage-specific HRV differences are well-documented (LF/HF varies 3-5x); expect coverage deviation of 3-8% between states.
minimum_data_needed: Physiological recordings with concurrent polysomnography or actigraphy state labels
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in REM sleep segments will deviate > 6% from nominal when calibrated on pooled NREM+wake data, but < 2% when calibrated on REM-only data.
cards.failure_condition: State-stratified conformal prediction does not improve coverage stability compared to pooled (paired t-test p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired comparison: per-state coverage deviation (pooled vs. stratified calibration) across subjects; Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
cards.falsification_test: Train a state classifier on residuals; if classifier cannot distinguish states (AUC ~ 0.5), residuals are exchangeable across states, falsifying the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation in physiological signals violates the exchangeability assumption of split conformal prediction, causing coverage to degrade with increasing segment length.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Strong temporal autocorrelation in physiological signals (e.g., HRV, respiratory sinus arrhythmia) means consecutive samples are not exchangeable; longer segments contain fewer effective independent samples, inflating conformal quantile variance.
cards.causal_path: Segment Length -> Effective Sample Size (n_eff = n / (1 + 2*sum(autocorr))) -> Conformal Quantile Variance -> Coverage Instability (under-coverage for long segments, over-coverage for short)
control_variables: Use dependent conformal prediction (e.g., CV+ with block CV)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability with segment length is due to finite-sample effects (small n), not autocorrelation specifically.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation follows 1/sqrt(n) scaling regardless of autocorrelation structure.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage deviation vs. segment length for original residuals vs. phase-randomized surrogates (preserves spectrum but destroys temporal structure); autocorrelation mechanism predicts different curves.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Typical HRV autocorrelation at lag-1 is 0.7-0.9; effective sample size reduction of 3-10x should cause measurable quantile variance inflation.
minimum_data_needed: Long continuous recordings (>=30 min) with ground truth
Residual time series from base predictor
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage deviation from nominal scales with 1/sqrt(n_eff) not 1/sqrt(n); segments with autocorrelation > 0.8 show 2x larger deviation than phase-randomized surrogates at same nominal length.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage deviation vs. segment length fits 1/sqrt(n) equally well as 1/sqrt(n_eff) (AIC difference < 2).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Nonlinear regression: coverage_deviation ~ a / sqrt(n_eff) + b; compare AIC to model with n instead of n_eff.
cards.falsification_test: Apply block conformal prediction with block size > autocorrelation decay time; if coverage stabilizes, autocorrelation was the mechanism. If instability persists, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Inconsistent ground truth labeling across annotators or algorithms for different physiological segments introduces label noise that masquerades as coverage instability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Segment-specific labeling protocols (e.g., manual scoring for sleep vs. algorithmic for wake) create heterogeneous label noise distributions; conformal prediction calibrates to noisy labels, causing apparent coverage deviation when evaluated against a different reference.
cards.causal_path: Segment Type -> Labeling Method (Manual/Algorithmic/Heuristic) -> Label Noise Distribution (Bias, Variance) -> Calibration to Noisy Target -> Evaluation Against Clean Reference -> Apparent Coverage Deviation
mechanism_variables: Label Noise Variance (estimated via inter-rater ICC)
control_variables: Use only segments with consensus labeling
Model label noise explicitly (e.g., conformal with noisy labels)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is genuine model performance variation across segments, not a labeling artifact.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation persists when evaluated against consensus labels from multiple expert annotators.
cards.distinguishing_test: Re-evaluate coverage using a held-out expert consensus label set; labeling-noise mechanism predicts deviation disappears, genuine mechanism predicts deviation persists.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Inter-rater ICC for sleep staging is ~0.8; for respiratory event scoring ~0.7. This noise level can shift empirical coverage by 5-15% depending on noise structure.
minimum_data_needed: Segments with multiple independent label sources (>=3 raters or algorithms)
cards.testable_prediction: Segments labeled by low-ICC methods (ICC < 0.75) show coverage deviation > 8% from nominal when evaluated against high-ICC consensus, while high-ICC segments (ICC > 0.9) show deviation < 3%.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage deviation remains > 5% even when evaluated against multi-rater consensus labels (p > 0.05 for reduction).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test: coverage deviation (original labels vs. consensus labels) across segments; test mean difference > 0.
cards.falsification_test: Simulate label noise matching estimated ICC; if simulated noise reproduces observed coverage deviation pattern, labeling is sufficient explanation. If not, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Improper segmentation strategy (fixed-length windows ignoring physiological boundaries) mixes distinct dynamical regimes, creating heterogeneous calibration sets that yield unstable coverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Fixed-duration segmentation cuts across physiological events (e.g., apneas, arousals, ectopic beats), mixing segments with different error distributions; the resulting calibration set quantile represents a mixture that fits no single regime well.
cards.causal_path: Segmentation Strategy (Fixed vs. Event-Aligned) -> Regime Purity (Entropy of Physiological State within Segment) -> Residual Distribution Homogeneity -> Calibration Quantile Representativeness -> Coverage Stability
mechanism_variables: Regime Purity Index (0-1, based on state annotation homogeneity)
Residual Distribution KL Divergence (within-segment vs. calibration)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is due to inherent physiological variability, not segmentation artifacts; event-aligned segmentation won't help.
cards.rival_prediction: Event-aligned and fixed-length segmentation show similar coverage deviation distributions.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage deviation variance across segments for fixed vs. event-aligned segmentation; segmentation mechanism predicts lower variance for event-aligned.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Fixed windows mixing apnea/non-apnea segments can create bimodal residual distributions; expect 30-50% reduction in coverage deviation variance with proper alignment.
minimum_data_needed: Physiological recordings with event annotations (apneas, arousals, beats)
cards.testable_prediction: Variance of per-segment coverage deviation across a recording is > 40% lower with event-aligned segmentation than with fixed 30s windows.
cards.failure_condition: Levene's test for equality of coverage deviation variances between segmentation methods shows p > 0.05.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Levene's test on per-segment coverage deviations (fixed vs. event-aligned) across multiple recordings.
cards.falsification_test: Generate synthetic data with known regime boundaries; if event-aligned segmentation fails to stabilize coverage on synthetic data where regimes are perfectly known, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Finite calibration set size combined with high-dimensional physiological feature spaces causes conformal quantile estimation error that varies systematically with segment feature density.
cards.proposed_mechanism: In high-dimensional feature spaces (e.g., raw waveform + HRV + spectral features), the calibration set sparsely covers the feature space; segments in low-density regions have fewer similar calibration points, leading to quantile estimation error and coverage deviation.
cards.causal_path: Segment Feature Vector -> Calibration Set Local Density (k-NN distance in feature space) -> Local Quantile Estimation Error -> Coverage Deviation (under-coverage in sparse regions)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage deviation in sparse regions is due to genuine model extrapolation error, not quantile estimation error.
cards.rival_prediction: Model prediction error (MAE) increases in sparse regions, but conformal quantile correctly captures this (coverage remains nominal).
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage deviation vs. local density for conformal prediction vs. oracle quantile (computed from large test set); quantile-estimation mechanism predicts deviation only for conformal, not oracle.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Depends on intrinsic dimensionality of physiological feature manifold; need pilot data estimating covering numbers. Would estimate via: fit k-NN density on calibration features, regress coverage deviation on log-density, extrapolate to target n_cal.
minimum_data_needed: Large calibration set (n_cal >= 5000) with high-dimensional features (d >= 50)
Independent large test set for oracle quantile estimation
cards.testable_prediction: Segments in lowest density decile show coverage deviation > 7% from nominal; highest density decile shows deviation < 2%. Oracle quantile shows < 2% deviation across all deciles.
cards.failure_condition: Oracle quantile shows similar coverage deviation pattern as conformal quantile across density deciles (correlation > 0.7).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression: coverage_deviation ~ log(local_density); test slope < 0 for conformal but not for oracle.
cards.falsification_test: Increase calibration set size 10x via data augmentation (if valid) or collection; if coverage deviation in sparse regions does not decrease proportionally to 1/sqrt(n_cal), mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian modulation of physiological signal-to-noise ratio creates time-of-day-dependent residual distributions that violate conformal prediction's exchangeability assumption across segments recorded at different times.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Circadian rhythms modulate both signal amplitude (e.g., cortisol-driven BP changes) and noise (e.g., movement artifacts during wake), creating systematic time-of-day variation in residual variance that a single calibration quantile cannot capture.
cards.causal_path: Time of Day -> Circadian Phase (melatonin/cortisol proxy) -> Signal Amplitude & Artifact Rate -> Residual Variance -> Conformal Quantile Mismatch -> Coverage Deviation by Time Bin
mechanism_variables: Circadian Phase Proxy (core body temp minimum offset)
control_variables: Include circadian phase as difficulty score in weighted conformal
cards.rival_explanation: Time-of-day coverage variation is mediated entirely by sleep/wake state, not direct circadian effects.
cards.rival_prediction: Controlling for sleep/wake state eliminates time-of-day coverage variation.
cards.distinguishing_test: Within same sleep state (e.g., NREM only), test if coverage still varies by circadian phase; circadian mechanism predicts yes, sleep-state mechanism predicts no.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Circadian HRV amplitude is ~10-15% peak-to-trough; residual variance modulation likely smaller. Expect 1-3% coverage deviation across circadian phases.
minimum_data_needed: Circadian phase markers (core body temp or dim-light melatonin onset)
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in 04:00-08:00 bin (circadian trough) deviates > 2% from nominal when calibrated on pooled data, but < 1% when calibrated on same-phase data.
cards.failure_condition: Time-of-day coverage variation becomes non-significant (p > 0.05) after including sleep/wake state as covariate.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-way ANOVA: coverage ~ time_bin * sleep_state; test time_bin main effect after accounting for sleep_state.
cards.falsification_test: Simulate residuals with only sleep-state-dependent variance (no circadian component); if this reproduces observed time-of-day pattern, circadian mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Conformal prediction's marginal coverage guarantee fails to provide conditional coverage across physiological signal segments with different difficulty levels, causing systematic under-coverage on hard segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Marginal conformal prediction guarantees average coverage but not coverage conditional on segment difficulty (e.g., low SNR, arrhythmia burden); hard segments systematically fall below nominal coverage while easy segments exceed it.
cards.causal_path: Segment Difficulty (SNR, Arrhythmia Burden, Morphology Complexity) -> Conditional Error Distribution -> Marginal Quantile Mismatch for Hard Segments -> Conditional Coverage Deviation (Under-coverage on Hard, Over-coverage on Easy)
mechanism_variables: Segment Difficulty Score (composite: SNR, % ectopic beats, spectral entropy)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage is stable across difficulty; apparent variation is sampling noise from finite test segments per bin.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation across difficulty bins is not statistically significant; confidence intervals overlap nominal.
cards.distinguishing_test: Test for trend in coverage vs. difficulty bins (Cochran-Armitage); marginal coverage mechanism predicts significant negative trend.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Theoretical results show marginal conformal can have conditional coverage as low as 0% on hard subsets; empirical studies on medical data show 10-20% gaps between easy/hard.
minimum_data_needed: Segments with difficulty annotations (SNR, arrhythmia labels)
Base model predictions and ground truth
cards.testable_prediction: Hardest difficulty decile shows coverage < 80% at nominal 90%; easiest decile shows coverage > 95%. Coverage gap > 10%.
cards.failure_condition: Cochran-Armitage trend test for coverage vs. difficulty bins shows p > 0.05.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Cochran-Armitage trend test on coverage across 10 difficulty bins; logistic regression: covered ~ difficulty_score.
cards.falsification_test: Apply Mondrian conformal prediction with difficulty bins; if conditional coverage equalizes across bins, marginal coverage was the mechanism. If gaps persist, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Environmental electromagnetic interference (EMI) from medical equipment creates segment-specific artifact bursts that violate the exchangeability assumption by introducing non-physiological outliers in the calibration set.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Intermittent EMI (e.g., from electrosurgical units, MRI gradients, wireless devices) contaminates specific segments with high-amplitude artifacts; these outliers inflate the conformal quantile, causing over-coverage on clean segments and under-coverage on EMI-contaminated segments if artifacts differ in character.
cards.causal_path: EMI Event Occurrence -> Artifact Amplitude & Spectral Signature -> Residual Outlier Generation -> Calibration Quantile Inflation -> Coverage Deviation (Over-coverage on Clean, Under-coverage on EMI if Model Fails Differently)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage variation is due to physiological state changes coinciding with EMI events (e.g., surgery), not EMI itself.
cards.rival_prediction: EMI flag adds no predictive power for coverage deviation beyond physiological state variables.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage on EMI-flagged vs. clean segments matched on physiological state (same sleep stage, activity level); EMI mechanism predicts difference persists.
cards.effect_size_rationale: EMI artifacts can exceed physiological signals 10-100x; even brief contamination (1-2% of samples) can shift 90th percentile quantile substantially.
minimum_data_needed: Recordings with synchronized EMI spectral monitoring
cards.testable_prediction: EMI-contaminated segments show coverage deviation > 5% from clean segments matched on physiological state; robust conformal (90th percentile of clean calibration) restores coverage on clean segments to within 1%.
cards.failure_condition: Matched-pair comparison of EMI vs. clean segments shows no significant coverage difference (paired t-test p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Matched-pair design: each EMI segment matched to clean segment with same physiological state; paired t-test on coverage deviation.
cards.falsification_test: Inject synthetic EMI artifacts into clean segments at known rates; if coverage deviation pattern matches observed data only when injection mimics real EMI spectral/temporal structure, mechanism confirmed. If any artifact injection reproduces pattern, mechanism is falsified (non-specific artifact effect).
